workflow_metadata.name: Feature Update Workflow
workflow_metadata.description: Handle changes to existing systems with foundational alignment validation and functional architecture refinement
workflow_metadata.purpose: Safely update existing systems while maintaining architectural integrity
workflow_metadata.v2_improvements: Added functional architecture phase before system allocation to prevent rework and ensure complete functional definition

required_conditions: System currently deployed or in development

feature_or_service_change.description: User wants to change or add features to existing system

context_management.description: Prevent context drift and token exhaustion during workflow execution

rag_enhanced_mode.description: RECOMMENDED - Use RAG for automatic context injection and degradation detection
rag_enhanced_mode.benefits: Automatic context refresh, degradation detection, token-efficient retrieval
rag_enhanced_mode.fallback: If RAG not set up, use manual operations counter and refresh sequence below

operations_counter.rule: Increment after each real operation (file modification, tool execution, validation)

degradation_signals_watch_for: Creating breaking changes without version increment
refresh_sequence_summary: 2. VERIFY PWD - Confirm in correct directory
3. SAVE STATE - Update working_memory.json and step_progress_tracker.json
4. RELOAD - Read workflow file, existing architecture, change proposal
6. CONFIRM - State system name, service being updated, change type, next action
pre_operation_checklist: Verify creating new version, not overwriting old

self_improvement.description: Continuous workflow improvement through observation and metrics

during_execution.document: Log observations to context/process_log.md with timestamps

workflow_steps.name: Change Proposal & Impact Analysis
workflow_steps.description: Analyze proposed changes and assess impact on existing architecture

actions.purpose: Ensure changes align with system mission, user scenarios, success criteria

gates.name: Foundational Alignment Gate
gates.note: MANDATORY gate - cannot proceed without foundational alignment

workflow_steps.name: Functional Architecture Analysis, Visualization & Stakeholder Validation
workflow_steps.description: Define complete functional architecture with human-readable visualizations and stakeholder validation BEFORE allocating to systems
workflow_steps.rationale: Defining WHAT the system must do (functions) with visual stakeholder validation before HOW it does it (system allocation) prevents rework, gaps, inefficiencies, and redundancies

actions.description: Document required functional flows for proposed changes
includes: Process flows showing sequence of operations
Decision flows showing branching logic and conditions
Changed flows highlighted (showing delta from current architecture)
actions.note: Focus on functional changes, not system/service changes

actions.description: Identify all required functions (complete functional decomposition)
actions.method: Break down each flow into discrete functions
outputs: List of all functions the system must perform
actions.note: Functions are WHAT the system does, not WHICH service does it

actions.purpose: CRITICAL: Create visual diagrams to show stakeholders the proposed functional changes
actions.rationale: Visual diagrams are essential for stakeholders to understand and validate proposed changes before implementation
actions.priority: HIGH - Must complete before technical analysis to enable stakeholder feedback
outputs: docs/diagrams/functional/process_flows_proposed.svg - Proposed process flows with changes highlighted
docs/diagrams/functional/decision_trees_proposed.svg - Decision trees with new branches highlighted
diagram_standards: Use standard notation (BPMN for process flows, UML for data flows)
Highlight changes in color (green for additions, orange for modifications, red for removals)
Show before/after views for modified flows
actions.note: These visualizations will be reviewed with stakeholders in FU-01A-A04

actions.description: Stakeholder review of functional architecture visualizations
actions.purpose: Validate proposed functional changes with stakeholders before committing to implementation
review_artifacts: Delta visualization showing current vs. proposed
review_questions: Do the proposed functional changes solve the stated problem?
Are there unintended side effects or impacts?
Are all affected workflows and processes captured?
Do the changes align with user expectations?
Is the scope of change appropriate (not too large, not too small)?
outputs: Refined functional requirements based on feedback
actions.blocking: If major issues found, refine and re-review
actions.success_criteria: Stakeholders validate that proposed functional architecture addresses needs and has no major gaps

actions.purpose: Generate graph for automated analysis and gap detection
actions.note: This graph represents FUNCTIONS for technical analysis

actions.description: Analyze functional architecture for technical issues
analysis_types: Gap detection: Missing functions needed to complete flows
Redundancy detection: Duplicate or overlapping functions
Inefficiency detection: Circular flows, excessive handoffs
Completeness check: All user scenarios covered by functions

actions.description: Iterative functional architecture refinement with stakeholder and technical validation
actions.pattern: MANDATORY LOOP - Combines stakeholder feedback AND technical analysis

loop_structure.step_1: Review stakeholder feedback (FU-01A-A04) AND technical analysis issues (FU-01A-A06)
loop_structure.step_2: Categorize issues by severity and source
loop_structure.step_2a: Stakeholder issues: Scope concerns, missing functions, misalignment with expectations
loop_structure.step_3: Refine functional architecture to address critical issues from both sources
loop_structure.step_4: Regenerate BOTH human visualizations (FU-01A-A03) AND machine graph (FU-01A-A05)
loop_structure.step_5: Re-run stakeholder review (FU-01A-A04) AND technical analysis (FU-01A-A06)
loop_structure.step_6: If critical issues remain from EITHER source, LOOP back to step_1
loop_structure.termination: Loop until BOTH stakeholder validation passes AND technical analysis passes

success_criteria: No redundant functions (each function serves unique purpose)
No inefficient flows (minimal handoffs, no circular dependencies)
All decision points have complete logic branches

actions.description: Validate functional architecture against change proposal
checks: All proposed changes reflected in functional architecture
Functional architecture aligns with foundational documents
No functional gaps that would prevent feature from working

actions.purpose: Create human-readable diagrams of functional flows

outputs: Stakeholder sign-off on proposed functional changes

gates.name: Functional Architecture Completeness & Stakeholder Validation Gate
checks: - Stakeholders reviewed and approved functional architecture visualizations
- Change deltas clearly communicated through visual diagrams
- Proposed changes align with stakeholder expectations
- All user scenarios covered by functions
- All decision points have complete logic
- Functional architecture graph analysis shows coherence
- Change proposal fully reflected in functional architecture
- Complete set of human-readable diagrams showing proposed changes
- Delta visualizations showing current vs. proposed
- Change impact clearly highlighted in diagrams
gates.note: Cannot proceed to functional allocation until BOTH stakeholder validation passes AND technical analysis confirms completeness. Human visualizations with change deltas are MANDATORY for stakeholder communication.

workflow_steps.transition_note: Now that WHAT the system must do is defined (functional architecture), proceed to HOW it does it (functional allocation to systems in FU-02)

workflow_steps.name: Functional Allocation & System Architecture Re-Engineering
workflow_steps.description: Allocate functions to systems and update system architecture to accommodate changes

actions.description: Functional Allocation - Assign functions to systems/services
actions.purpose: Map each function from functional architecture (FU-01A) to specific services
allocation_criteria: Group related functions into services (high cohesion)
Respect existing service boundaries where appropriate
Identify new services if needed for new functions
actions.validation: Ensure all functions from functional architecture are allocated to services

actions.description: Update affected service_architecture.json files using VERSIONING based on functional allocation
actions.versioning_workflow: Follow SE-07 (Architecture Evolution) workflow for each affected service
actions.note: Service updates driven by functional allocation from FU-02-A00

semantic_versioning_decision.determine_version_increment: Based on impact analysis from FU-01-A03
semantic_versioning_decision.major: If breaking changes identified → increment major version (v1.x.x → v2.0.0)
semantic_versioning_decision.minor: If new capabilities added (non-breaking) → increment minor (v1.0.x → v1.1.0)
semantic_versioning_decision.patch: If bug fixes or clarifications only → increment patch (v1.0.0 → v1.0.1)

procedure.step_1: Determine version increment for each affected service
procedure.step_3: Copy current version and make changes in new file
procedure.step_4: Update symlink to point to new version
procedure.step_5: Update version_manifest.json (add new version entry, update latest_version)

actions.reference: See SE-07 in systems_engineering workflow for detailed versioning procedures

actions.note: Interface registry typically has single version, but can be versioned if major system-wide interface changes

actions.description: Update human-readable documentation with new version
actions.pairing_rule: Human doc version MUST match architecture version exactly
actions.symlink_update: Update system_description.md symlink to point to new version
actions.reference: See AV-03-A02 in artifacts workflow for human doc versioning
includes: Document what changed from previous version

actions.note: Validates via symlinks, so validates new version
Uses symlinks from index.json, so automatically reflects new versions
actions.purpose: Update graph to reflect architecture changes

actions.description: Update implementation to match new architecture
actions.pattern: Follow development workflow steps as needed

actions.description: Update tests to cover new functionality

workflow_steps.name: Integration, Validation & Release Preparation
workflow_steps.description: Validate changes and prepare for release

completion.description: Feature update workflow complete - changes validated and ready for release
next_steps: Deploy to production per release process

critical_reminders: ALWAYS run validate_foundational_alignment.py before proceeding (gate G-FU-01 is MANDATORY)
ALWAYS complete functional architecture (FU-01A) with visualization and stakeholder validation BEFORE functional allocation (FU-02)
Define WHAT the system does (functions) before HOW it does it (system allocation)
HUMAN-READABLE VISUALIZATIONS WITH CHANGE DELTAS ARE MANDATORY (FU-01A-A03): Show current vs. proposed using BPMN/UML diagrams
STAKEHOLDER REVIEW IS MANDATORY (FU-01A-A04): Validate change visualizations with stakeholders BEFORE proceeding
Use system_of_systems_graph_v2.py to analyze functional architecture for gaps, redundancies, inefficiencies
Iterate on functional architecture with BOTH stakeholder feedback AND technical analysis (FU-01A-A07 loop is MANDATORY)
Version all updated service_architecture.json files (don't overwrite)
Ensure functional allocation matrix maps ALL functions to services
Highlight breaking changes clearly in delta report and visualizations
Run regression testing to catch unintended side effects
common_mistakes: Jumping directly to system allocation without functional architecture (causes rework)
Creating only machine-readable JSON without human visualizations showing change deltas
Skipping stakeholder review of functional architecture visualizations
Not creating BPMN/UML diagrams showing current vs. proposed changes
Proceeding to FU-02 without stakeholder sign-off on proposed changes
Not iterating visualization based on stakeholder feedback
Incomplete functional architecture (missing functions, gaps in flows)
Not using system_of_systems_graph_v2.py to analyze functional architecture
Proceeding to FU-02 with functional architecture issues unresolved (either stakeholder OR technical)
Forgetting to create functional allocation matrix
Overwriting old architecture versions instead of creating new versions

workflow_philosophy.two_phase_approach: Functional Architecture with Visualization (WHAT) → Functional Allocation (HOW)
workflow_philosophy.phase_1_functional_architecture: Define complete functional architecture for proposed changes. CRITICAL: Create human-readable visualizations showing change deltas (current vs. proposed). Review with stakeholders using diagrams. Iterate with stakeholder feedback AND technical analysis until both validate.
workflow_philosophy.phase_2_functional_allocation: Allocate functions to systems/services. Update system architectures with versioning. Use UAF or other frameworks for system definition.
workflow_philosophy.visualization_critical: Human-readable visualizations (BPMN, UML) with change deltas are MANDATORY. Stakeholders must see and approve proposed changes visually before implementation begins.
workflow_philosophy.benefits: Prevents rework from incomplete requirements, validates changes with stakeholders before implementation, finds architectural issues early through stakeholder AND technical validation, ensures complete functional coverage, reduces redundancy and inefficiency, prevents scope creep and misalignment
workflow_philosophy.lesson_learned: Jumping directly to system updates without functional architecture and stakeholder visualization causes issues later requiring revisiting service definitions. Visual stakeholder validation prevents costly misalignment between expectations and implementation.

mandatory_gates: G-FU-01 (Foundational Alignment Gate) - cannot proceed without foundational alignment

G-FU-01A (Functional Architecture Completeness & Stakeholder Validation Gate) - cannot proceed to functional allocation until functional architecture is complete, visualized with change deltas, stakeholder-approved, and technically validated
